title: Ops flow composer and smart pager throttling for regional surge
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: During partial regional degradation and bursty traffic patterns we observe high paging noise from transient timeouts (client retries + cold starts + autoscale churn). Pager fatigue reduces engineer responsiveness and increases mean time to mitigation for real SLO breaches. Goal: Build an "ops flow composer" and smart pager-throttling layer that reduces false-positive pages while preserving rapid escalation for real cross-region SLO degradation. Scope: alert throttling, contextual dedupe (by region & route), integration with circuit-breaker states and load-shedding signals, canonical on-call runbook templates, and automation hooks for safe mitigation (scaled rollback, traffic steering). Out of scope: changes to billing metrics or customer-visible rate limits.
acceptance_criteria: Alert volume for transient regional API 5xx events reduced by >=60% in steady-state (measured over 7d) without delaying pages for true SLO breaches.
On-call flows provide a single consolidated page per incident window per region with clear remediation steps and an automatic escalation at 15 minutes if SLO threshold still breached.
Circuit-breaker state (open/half-open) and load-shed signals are visible in the page payload and the Console incident UI.
Canary rollout completed across 2 customer-facing regions with metrics dashboards and a rollback path documented in the runbook.
Automated runbook actions (traffic reweight to healthy region) are behind an opt-in toggle and require two-step confirmation in the console for production clusters.
implementation_notes: Design: Add an 'ops flow composer' service that ingests alert signals and metadata (region, route, model, instance group, cb-state) and emits deduplicated notifications using rewrite rules and scoring.

Thresholds: Use SLO burn-rate + regional error-rate sliding window (1m/5m/30m) to decide immediate page vs batched summary. Fast-path pages when burn-rate > 3x for 1m AND client-visible p99 latency > configured SLO.
Circuit breakers: Treat CB-open events as low-noise (informational) unless accompanied by increased consumer error percentage — avoid automatic pages for dependent downstream CB transitions.

Load-shedding integration: When autoscaler or admission controller emits 'load-shed' tags, mark alerts with 'operational-shed' and route to a separate, lower-noise channel (Ops-Shed) with longer aggregation windows.
Dedupe keys: {service, region, route_group, model_variant} with time-windowed merging (default 10 minutes) and a cap of one high-priority page per 15 minutes per region.
Notification channels: Primary: PagerDuty high/critical; Secondary: Slack Ops channel for summaries; Tertiary: Email digest for non-urgent low-noise clusters.
Rollback & safety: Provide a 'circuit-breaker escalate' action in the Console that performs traffic reweighting with preflight checks and requires two SRE approvals for clusters with >1k throughput.
Data retention: Store composed alert events for 90 days for retrospective analysis and ML-based tuning.
Testing: Synthetic chaos tests (partial AZ/region fail) and load spikes to validate dedupe rules; unit tests for composer scoring logic.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy composer to staging and Canary region (us-west-2) and route 5% of alert traffic. Run for 2 weeks and compare page counts vs baseline.
Phase 2 (Selective opt-in): Allow team-level opt-in for non-critical clusters; measure impact for 7 days and collect on-call feedback.
Phase 3 (Global): Gradual enablement across remaining regions in pairs, monitoring error budget burn and mean time to acknowledge (MTTA).
Kill switch: Global 'disable-composer' toggle that immediately forwards raw alerts to legacy pipeline for 30m while we investigate.
Post-rollout: 30-day observation window with daily dashboard and weekly retrospectives; iterate thresholds based on incident learnings.
monitoring_and_alerts: SLOs: request_success_rate per region (1m burn, 5m, 30m), p99 latency per region; set burn-rate thresholds for actionability.
Noise metrics: pages_per_region_per_hour, unique_incidents_per_region, duplicate_alert_rate; target duplicate_alert_rate < 0.15.
Alert lifecyle metrics: MTTA, MTTR, escalation_rate, runbook_action_success_rate.
Dashboards: compose 'ops-composer/overview' dashboard in Console showing compose decisions, CB states, reweights executed, and affected customers.
Synthetic tests: periodic canary traffic spike every 6 hours to validate that composer does not suppress legitimate pages.
